stories.title: Naqvi complicated provinces debate by 'irrelevant speech at irrelevant forum', says Rana Sanaullah
summary: PML-N Senator Rana Sanaullah on Monday said Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi “complicated” the matter of creating new provinces by making an “irrelevant speech at an irrelevant forum”.

[But] he chose the wrong method, the wrong procedure, the wrong forum, and then made such a speech right at its inception that the whole system collapsed,” Sanaullah said, observing that those remarks had diverted attention away from the actual debate of new provinces.

Sanaullah also commented on Bilawal’s stance that neither he nor his father, President Asif Ali Zardari, had been approached by the government about the matter after the debate began. “Then what have you (Naqvi) been doing for four months?

stories.title: Pemra bans ads, promotions for commercial infant formula on electronic media
summary: According to an order issued by Pemra, the decision was taken following a letter from the Ministry of National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination dated Nov 18, regarding implementation of the Protection of Breastfeeding and Child Nutrition Ordinance 2002.

The committee also reviewed relevant provisions of the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan Act 2012, the Pemra Ordinance 2002 and the Pemra Electronic Media (Programmes and Advertisements) Code of Conduct 2015.

Invoking Section 27 of the Pemra Ordinance 2002, the authority declared that “advertisement(s) of infant formula products (commercially manufactured formula powder milk) shall be prohibited forthwith”.

stories.title: ‘Rights at stake, not privileges’: Opposition leaders write to SC, FCC, IHC chief justices on Imran, Bushra’s health
summary: In an open letter to the same three judges last week, Imran appealed for medical treatment for himself and Bushra Bibi.

It also demanded that a writ of mandamus be issued regarding the non-implementation of the SC’s Aug 18 order for shifting Imran to Shifa International Hospital, and the concerns regarding Imran and Bushra Bibi’s health and detention.

On Aug 18, the SC directed the government to shift the jailed ex-premier to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad, a day after the superintendent of the Adiala jail — where Imran is imprisoned — submitted a report to the court on the ex-premier’s health condition.

stories.title: AB de Villiers makes new claim about Australian 'Sandpapergate' ball-tampering scandal
summary: Former South African batsman AB de Villiers has alleged that Australia engaged in ball-tampering from the first match of their 2018 “Sandpapergate” tour of South Africa.

De Villiers alleged in a post on his YouTube channel that the ball-tampering, which culminated in Cameron Bancroft being caught using sandpaper in the third Test in Cape Town, actually began in the first Test in Durban.
Absolutely no doubt in my mind.” He added: “We lost that first Test match in Durban with the ball reversing at a very, very interesting time.

stories.title: 'No national security risk': Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after affair scandal
summary: Nvidia on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior US government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal.

Trump, who had previously called on the AI giant to reinstate Huang, congratulated him in a post on Truth Social. “The Nvidia board of directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO.

Alice Huang had contact with China spy agency: NYT Alice Huang, the alleged spy at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, was in touch with an official from China’s top spy agency during an affair with the chip giant’s former chief executive, the New York Times reported on Sunday.

stories.title: Peshawar to host opening ceremony, inaugural match for 12th edition of PSL: PCB chief
summary: PESHAWAR: Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) Chairman Mohsin Naqvi said on Monday that Peshawar will host the opening ceremony and the inaugural match for the 12th edition of the HBL Pakistan Super League (PSL) scheduled for next year.

The announcement by Naqvi came shortly after Kundi — whose administration now runs the province under governor’s rule — said the name of Arbab Niaz Stadium would be restored, reversing the PTI government’s decision to rename it to Imran Khan Stadium.
Peshawar was supposed to host a PSL match on March 28 in the previous edition, but matches were restricted to Karachi and Lahore as part of austerity measures after the US-Iran war broke out.

stories.title: Pakistan has Portugal's 'full support' for GSP+ status, visiting FM says during talks in Islamabad
summary: Pakistan has Portugal’s “full support” for the European Union’s (EU) GSP+ status, Portuguese Minister of State and Foreign Affairs Paulo Rangel said on Monday during delegation-level talks between the two countries held in Islamabad.

He proposed the establishment of a Pakistan-Portugal joint working group on trade and investment to address trade barriers, identify opportunities and facilitate commercial cooperation, the statement added.

PM Shehbaz invites Portuguese investment at business forum FM Rangel also met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, who appreciated Portugal’s acceptance of Pakistan’s offer to establish a JMC for a multisectoral partnership.

stories.title: Bilawal calls for restoring supremacy of Parliament and trust in judiciary, electoral system
summary: PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Monday called for restoring the supremacy of Parliament as well as trust in the judiciary and the electoral system.

We must restore confidence in our judiciary, and the election system we have, we must restore trust in it now.” Bilawal’s remarks come as the debate over a “system reset” in the country has intensified over the past few months.
The youth [of Pakistan] want to see a country where there is no corruption.

stories.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang — the indispensable godfather of AI
summary: Chips designed by Nvidia push the boundaries of artificial intelligence, and its leather-jacket-wearing co-founder Jensen Huang built the company into one of the world’s most important brands over his 33 years at the helm.

Huang, 63, reportedly had an affair with Alice Huang — who is of no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, which is under investigation for allegedly helping Chinese firms gain access to Nvidia’s top-line chips.
Nvidia had taken care to project a drama-free image of Huang.

stories.title: MQM-P to deliberate on PPP’s request to postpone Nov 29 Karachi rally, says Farooq Sattar
summary: Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) leader Dr Farooq Sattar said on Monday that the party would deliberate on a PPP request to postpone its Nov 29 rally in Karachi, to be held in support of new provinces.
He maintained that the MQM-P’s demand for new provinces was not limited to Sindh or Karachi but extended to the entire country.
Siddiqui also questioned the PPP’s opposition to the creation of new provinces, alleging that Karachi’s contribution to Sindh’s budget was behind the party’s resistance.

stories.title: Building near Karachi Press Club evacuated due to hoax bomb threat
summary: KARACHI: A bomb threat at a building near Karachi Press Club (KPC) drew a response from multiple authorities on Monday but was found to have been a hoax, according to police.
He said that two teams of bomb experts conducted a search of the building premises and found it to be a hoax call.
Other areas of the building were also searched in response to the bomb threat, but no detonating or explosive material was found, he said.

stories.title: Meta AI chief says superintelligence is coming, warns next year will be critical
summary: Meta's chief AI officer Alexandr Wang has said that artificial intelligence capable of surpassing human intellect is on the way, warning that decisions over the next year will be critical to how humanity handles it. “Superintelligence is arriving.
How humanity acts over the next year will have great consequence on what future world we live in,” Wang wrote on X.
The 29-year-old executive was referring to AI systems that could outperform the best humans in virtually every field, including scientific research, problem-solving and technological development.

stories.title: Virginia, Oregon sue Musk's SpaceX over Grok AI's creation of child sexual abuse images
summary: Beginning in January, Grok told users that its image generation features were only for paying subscribers, which did not stop the images' creation but allowed the company to profit from them, the lawsuit said.
Lawsuits stack up over Grok SpaceX is facing more than a dozen ​lawsuits brought by individuals who say nonconsensual sexual images of them as minors or adults were generated by Grok.
In ​the UK, lawmaker Jess Asato ⁠is suing SpaceX after Grok users generated sexualized images of her.

stories.title: 'Total failure': Sanaullah blames Naqvi for mishandling new provinces issue
summary: Sanaullah further accused Naqvi of mishandling the issue of new provinces through his public statements, saying he had chosen the wrong forum and adopted an inappropriate approach.

Sanaullah said the matter had been complicated and made controversial over the past four months, adding that Naqvi, whom he described as the “worthy minister” who had led the initiative, should take responsibility for the situation.
Sanaullah again maintained that Naqvi had mishandled the issue of new provinces and that, now that it had become controversial, a way forward could perhaps be found through a referendum.

stories.title: Govt issues advisory to WhatsApp users, warns of 'multiple vulnerabilities'
summary: The National CERT advised government institutions, public and private organisations and individual users of WhatsApp to "update WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business on all platforms to the latest version from the official app store or the vendor’s website".

The advisory also recommended that users "identify installed versions" and not "install unofficial or modified WhatsApp clients or sideloaded builds, which are a source of crafted malicious messages".

On January 14, National CERT issued a nationwide advisory warning of a sharp rise in WhatsApp account hijacking incidents, saying the attacks were active, widespread and targeting users across all demographics.

stories.title: Let's get digital: Punjab introduces on-screen marking system with facial recognition for board exams
summary: LAHORE: The Punjab government has introduced a digital on-screen marking system with facial recognition to check examination papers in an effort to modernise the process and improve transparency across the province’s nine boards for intermediate and secondary education.

Talking to Dawn, the chairman of the Lahore Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dr Badar, said the digital marking system was being implemented in the ongoing second annual examinations across Punjab.
The system is also intended to bring greater uniformity to marking through standardised assessment criteria and digital monitoring of examiners.

stories.title: Naqvi calls on PM Shehbaz as debate on new provinces gains steam
summary: ISLAMABAD/LAHORE: Amid growing debate on the issue of creation of new provinces, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.

In Monday’s meeting, Naqvi and Shujaat discussed the overall political situation, measures to maintain law and order and the need to transfer power to the grassroots level, according to a statement issued by the interior ministry after the meeting.
Last week, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry insisted that a referendum on the formation of new provinces “will happen” amid the debate on new provinces.

stories.title: PTI's Zafar says Karachi can become separate province, Imran Khan favours new administrative units
summary: ISLAMABAD: PTI parliamentary leader in the Senate, Barrister Ali Zafar, on Monday said that Karachi – Pakistan’s most populous metropolis – could be made a new province, claiming that party founder and former prime minister Imran Khan was in favour of it.

Zafar said that the PTI founder had given a “straightforward instruction” regarding the formation of new provinces. “He (Imran) has said that as long as provinces are concerned, they should be made,” the PTI’s leader in the Senate said.
Turning to another question, Zafar said that PTI was a political party and the opinion of Imran would be sought if it is asked to vote on new provinces.

stories.title: Pakistani singer Mohsin Raza Khan, known as Bunny, dies aged 74
summary: Dr Ali said the arrangements for Bunny's funeral and burial were being finalised, as his son, Chengiz, is based in London.
Dr Ali said the family was waiting to hear from Bunny's son before proceeding with the burial.
Afridi said Bunny had no relatives in Pakistan and that his son had been informed in accordance with the singer's wishes.

stories.title: Govt cuts petrol by Rs3, keeps diesel unchanged for Nov 24
summary: The federal government on Monday decreased the price of petrol by Rs3 per litre while keeping the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) unchanged for November 24.
The latest revision comes after the government decreased the price of petrol by Rs1 while increasing high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs2 per litre till November 23.
Around 10 million two-wheeler users and 800,000 three-wheeler users would be entitled to relief on 20 litres of fuel per month, translating into a maximum monthly benefit of Rs2,000 per beneficiary.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz vows 'no cap' on homes for poor, sets Rs1,000b disbursement target under 'Apna Ghar' scheme
summary: Also Read: Housing finance doubles to Rs279b The prime minister added that the recognition also carried responsibility, as any delay in genuine loan approvals would now be attributed to them.

The premier also thanked Minister for Housing and Works Riaz Hussain Pirzada, Finance Minister Senator Muhammad Aurangzeb, the SBP governor and Minister for Economic Affairs Ahad Khan Cheema for their efforts, and appreciated Information Minister Attaullah Tarar’s publicity.
ABAD Chairman, Hanif Kohari, appreciated the prime minister for turning the housing initiative into a practical programme, and said it had created opportunities for the construction sector.

stories.title: Imran Khan may be engaged on new provinces if needed, says Tariq Fazal
summary: Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry on Monday said any decision on the creation of new provinces would be taken after consulting all political parties and stakeholders, adding that PTI founder Imran Khan could also be engaged if necessary.

Speaking on a private television programme, Capital Talk, Chaudhry questioned the Pakistan Peoples Party’s (PPP) reaction to the idea of a referendum, saying the Constitution clearly outlined the procedure for creating new provinces.
Chaudhry reiterated that any decision concerning new provinces would be made after taking all political parties and stakeholders into confidence.

stories.title: Analysis: Myanmar genocide judgment may bolster Gaza case against Israel
summary: South Africa, which has brought a genocide case against Israel over its conduct in Gaza, welcomed the judgment.
Important precedent Israeli legal scholar Yuval Shany said the ruling could broaden the arguments available to South Africa in its case against Israel.

Israel rejects those allegations and says its operations have been conducted in accordance with international law. “Arguments that a military intent or military objective would erase the idea that there could be a genocide intent are now rejected by the court,” said De Hoon.

stories.title: Marvel's final 'Doomsday' trailer hints at why three superhero worlds must unite
summary: Marvel Studios has released the final trailer for Avengers: Doomsday, offering another glimpse at the highly anticipated film featuring Robert Downey Jr. as the formidable Doctor Doom.

One of the major highlights of Avengers: Doomsday is the return of Chris Evans as Steve Rogers, marking another chapter for the former Captain America following his apparent retirement in 2019's Avengers: Endgame.
With Robert Downey Jr. taking on the role of Doctor Doom and several major Marvel teams joining forces, the film is set to bring together different corners of the superhero universe.

stories.title: Tajikistan becomes fourth country to withdraw from ICC since US diplomatic push
summary: Tajikistan has become the fourth country to formally begin withdrawing from the International ​Criminal Court since the US launched what it called a diplomatic ‌push to "dismantle the court", the presidency of the court's governing body said in a statement on Monday.

stories.title: 7 killed, 2 injured as stone-laden truck overturns onto mini-truck in Bahawalpur
summary: LAHORE: Seven people were killed and two others were injured when a stone-laden truck hit a mini-truck and overturned onto it in Bahawalpur’s Uch Sharif early on Monday morning, an official and Rescue 1122 said.
DPO Wahab said the driver of the stone-laden truck had fled the scene after the accident. “However, police have identified him and registered a case at Dhoorkot police station.
Earlier this month, a collision between a passenger bus and truck claimed the lives of 11 people and left 33 others injured near Pakpattan.

stories.title: Asif says process for referendum on new provinces likely to move forward early next year
summary: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif has said discussions on a possible referendum to create new provinces are expected to take a “definitive shape” by the end of this year, with the process likely to move forward early next year.

Asked whether the PML-N and the federal government had reached a principled decision on holding a referendum, and what its timeline and outline would be, he said: “Perhaps by the year-end, all this debate and discussion that is taking place will take some definitive shape.
The federal government, however, maintains that a referendum is a legal and constitutional means of gauging public opinion on the creation of new provinces.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia's influence loomed large over failed COP31 deal
summary: Read: COP31 ends without overarching deal Saudi Arabia and fellow members of the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries have long opposed climate language targeting fossil fuels, saying they need to ​be part of the global energy mix for the foreseeable future.
"It ​seems like when fossil fuels cannot be mentioned in the cover text, then somehow the oil countries have a larger voice at this COP," said Danish Climate Minister Samira Nawa.

The collapse of COP31 talks in Turkey on Sunday without a political agreement left exhausted negotiators questioning the future of a process that for three decades has led the global fight ​against climate change.

stories.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
summary: Nvidia on Monday said it was reinstating Jensen Huang as chief executive, effective immediately, an extraordinary reversal under pressure ​from US President Donald Trump following revelations of extramarital affairs ‌by Huang, including with an alleged Chinese spy.

Read: Trump backs potential return of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO The board's decision to bring Huang back highlights his deep influence over Nvidia and ​raises questions about how dependent one of the world's ​most valuable ⁠companies remains on its co-founder.
Rapid Response 47 shared the president's statement on X, "The Nvidia board of directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO.

stories.title: PPP asks MQM-P to reconsider Karachi rally dates at first meeting amid tensions over new provinces
summary: The Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) and Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) held their first face-to-face meeting on Monday following an escalation in tensions and exchange of heated statements over the proposed creation of new provinces.

Delegations from both parties met in the chamber of the opposition leader at the Sindh Assembly, with the PPP delegation requesting MQM-P to reconsider the dates of its planned rallies in Karachi on November 29 and December 6.
During the meeting, the PPP leaders urged MQM-P to postpone its planned rallies and hold them on another date, citing concerns about a possible law-and-order situation in the city.

stories.title: Bangladesh vows to arrest Hasina if she returns from India
summary: Bangladesh will arrest and jail former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina if she returns from India, a senior government minister said, as her plans to come home in December fuel political tension and renewed street violence.

Dhaka is instead seeking Hasina’s extradition from India, where she has lived since fleeing Bangladesh in 2024, and expects New Delhi to comply with an existing extradition treaty, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam told Reuters.
Obaed called for greater international pressure on Myanmar and the Arakan Army. “Bangladesh did not create this crisis.

stories.title: India to give $1.62bn economic package to flood-hit Nepal
summary: India will give Nepal an economic package worth 240 billion Nepalese rupees ($1.62bn), Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Monday, after talks with his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi.
The August 26 flood, caused by a glacier collapse on Nepal’s border with China, sent a mass of mud and rock crashing into the Trishuli river.
Nepal and India enjoy longstanding cultural, economic and people-to-people ties with an open border allowing hundreds of thousands of Nepalis to live and work in India.

stories.title: Fact check: Viral video of Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik accusing army of terrorism in Pakistan during India visit is doctored
summary: Multiple accounts shared a clip on social media platform X on November 21, 2026, allegedly showing Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik saying the army was behind terrorism in Pakistan during his speech at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi.

How it started On Nov 21, a satire and meme account using AI on X, according to its username, description and past posts, first shared a video allegedly showing Malik calling out the Pakistan Army for terrorism in Pakistan during his speech in New Delhi.

A reverse image search conducted to trace the original clip yielded a video uploaded on November 22, 2026, by Malik’s official YouTube channel with the title “Address at the First SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, New Delhi”.

stories.title: Ukraine claims strikes on two Russian boats off Libya
summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday said Ukraine was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, adding that one of them sank in the latest spillover from Moscow’s war with Kyiv.

But the United Nations condemned the strikes, warning against the prospect of a country still divided after the Libyan civil war becoming “a battleground for foreign conflicts”. “It all took place off the coast of Libya.
Libya’s eastern administration did not identify those responsible for the attack but said the country was “not a party to the Russian-Ukrainian war”.

stories.title: Peshawar to host PSL 12 matches
summary: Peshawar will host matches in the Pakistan Super League (PSL) for the first time when the tournament returns for its 12th edition with the city also set to stage the opening game, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) confirmed on Monday.
"Bringing the HBL PSL to Peshawar is about recognising what this city has given to Pakistan cricket and providing its people the chance to celebrate the game at home.

"Peshawar's love for cricket is unmatched and HBL PSL 12 will finally give that passion the stage it deserves." The PCB said the full schedule for PSL 12, including fixtures in Peshawar, would be announced in due course.

stories.title: 'Imran's life is in danger', opposition leaders urge top judges to intervene to protect ex-PM's health, fundamental rights
summary: Read: Jailed PTI founder seeks 'justice before it's too late' The Supreme Court, in a ruling on August 18, ordered that Imran be shifted to Shifa International Hospital for treatment and directed the government to arrange weekly meetings between him and his family.

The letter underscored that the Supreme Court order was "defeated within its first 72 hours", adding that on the "night of 20-21 August", Imran was taken not to Shifa International Hospital but to Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS).

Her medical records are being withheld from her family, and access to her doctors is restricted." The opposition leaders further urged the top courts to uphold the fundamental rights of Imran and Bushra: "The rights at stake are not privileges of a prisoner.

stories.title: ADB invests in Pakistan-based B2B fintech company Neem
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) on Monday said it invested an undisclosed amount in Neem, a Pakistan-based B2B fintech company that helps businesses receive, manage, and pay out money digitally.

Pakistan has made strong progress in digitising consumer payments, with the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP)’s instant payment system, Raast, and mobile wallets bringing millions of people onto digital rails.

Neem’s solutions are built to meet the payment needs of businesses of every size, including women-owned businesses and micro-entrepreneurs, so access to modern financial infrastructure is not limited to large enterprises.

stories.title: External networks sustaining militancy in Balochistan, study finds
summary: They interviewed 16 people working in security, counterterrorism, politics, governance, development, media, border management and the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC).
The study's central idea is that access to resources beyond Balochistan makes militant groups tougher and harder to dismantle.

According to the researchers, these narratives can do several things for militant groups: win political visibility, justify violence, attract sympathy, support recruitment, and cast development projects as something imposed from outside.

stories.title: Bilawal urges 'democratic reset' to rebuild public trust in parliament, judiciary and electoral process
summary: Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari on Monday called for a "democratic reset" to restore public confidence in state institutions, stressing that any effort to reform the country’s governance system must be rooted in democracy, unity and public trust.

Bilawal stressed that restoring public trust in the political and institutional system was essential for the country to move forward, calling for an approach that prioritised people's welfare over political divisions.

Sindh Youth Card At the ceremony, Bilawal also launched the Sindh Youth Card, describing it as an initiative to help young people enter the formal economy and access opportunities locally and internationally.
